project: Correct Stranded Recordings Replay and Artifact Delivery
description: Continue, or narrowly supersede and explicitly reconcile, PR #1779 so one canonical Recordings-owned replay/artifact capability is reachable from Factory Sessions runtime opening, artifact and legacy replay behavior is preserved, safe diagnostics and operation logging are directly owned, the complete valid/invalid behavior matrix is covered, the lowered coverage gate is restored, and the authoritative PR is merged.

context.customerAsk: Resolve exactly the four blocking findings on PR #1779: canonically inject and exercise the same narrow Recordings replay/artifact capability from Factory Sessions runtime opening, remove the dead parallel capability, restore directly owned safe diagnostics and operation logging, preserve legacy typed error identity and wrapping, and cover every listed valid and invalid runtime-opening case while preserving D1/D2 and delivering through actual merge.
context.problem: At exact head cf7241683c2b218b07bf5cad14e3da9f570c5884, the primary RecordingReplayArtifacts provider is unreachable while Factory Sessions receives a separately constructed ReplayInputCapability. The new operation lacks a directly owned structured diagnostic vocabulary and safe accepted-intent/terminal-outcome logs, changes the established legacy error wrapper to portable-replay context, omits required runtime-opening success/failure coverage, and lowers a Wire functional-coverage floor to accommodate the dead path.
context.solution: Consolidate portable-recording, legacy replay, and artifact behavior behind one narrow Recordings-owned capability implemented by an injected service and composed once in the canonical Wire graph. Inject that same authority into Factory Sessions runtime opening, remove the parallel and dead paths, publish safe owned diagnostics and structured operation logs, restore legacy typed wrapping, preserve detached/read-only and atomic artifact semantics, cover the complete runtime-opening matrix, restore the prior coverage floor, and clear all blockers on the exact authoritative head through merge.

packages: Recordings owns the single narrow replay/artifact operation, detached contracts, typed failures, structured diagnostics, artifact I/O policy, and operation logging.
Factory Sessions runtime opening consumes the injected Recordings capability and owns only conversion of detached replay facts into runtime-opening inputs.
Canonical Wire composition constructs and injects the one reachable authority and removes the overlapping dead/parallel provider path.
contracts: Directly own replay/artifact requests, results, identity, portable and legacy facts, diagnostics, and typed errors at the Recordings root.
Preserve errors.Is/errors.As behavior and distinct portable versus legacy wrapping, including load factory config: load replay artifact: ... for legacy loader failures.
Keep diagnostics detached and limited to stable code, area, safe logical field path, safe message, and supported-version facts.
changes.services: Implement the operation on one injected Recordings service with explicit read, legacy-load, atomic-publication, and structured-logger dependencies; introduce no service locator, dependency bag, secondary injector, runtime service factory, or parallel replay-input authority.
changes.api: No public CLI, HTTP, MCP, OpenAPI, Factory Event, or L1 Events-stream contract change is intended.
changes.tests: Add focused Recordings round-trip/read-only/diagnostic/log tests, Factory Sessions portable/legacy runtime-opening matrix tests, and behavior-driven canonical-composition coverage; restore the prior Wire coverage minimum and run typecheck, lint, short Go tests, required CI, exact-head review, conflict reconciliation, and merge.

acceptanceCriteria: Canonical application composition constructs one narrow Recordings replay/artifact capability and injects that same authority into Factory Sessions runtime opening; the primary behavior is reachable, the parallel replay-input authority is removed, and no dead provider or lowered coverage allowance remains.

A finalized recording can be exported, read, validated, and replay-loaded with stable identity, Factory Session scope, canonical event order, summaries, supported schema facts, detached results, read-only behavior, and existing atomic-publication semantics.

Portable and legacy runtime-opening successes retain their established runtime inputs and metadata, while every listed invalid case returns its stable typed classification, safe structured diagnostic, and zero partial result before replay execution or active session controls are constructed.

Legacy loader failures retain errors.Is/errors.As fidelity and the established load factory config: load replay artifact: ... wrapping context; portable failures retain their distinct portable context.

The owning replay/artifact operation emits structured accepted-intent and terminal-outcome logs plus safe diagnostics without exposing sensitive content or changing Factory Event, Events-stream, JSONL ledger, checkpoint, lifecycle, projection, or storage ownership.
Typecheck, formatting, lint, focused Recordings/Factory Sessions/composition tests, the restored coverage gate, the short Go suite, and all required CI are terminal and passing.

The implementation/review loop continues until all four blockers receive explicit clearance against the exact authoritative head, all blocking PR conversation feedback is addressed, shared-file and generated-Wire conflicts are reconciled, and the authoritative PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Use one replay and artifact authority in production
userStories.description: As a Factory Sessions maintainer, I want runtime opening to receive the one canonical Recordings replay/artifact capability so that historical input is loaded through a reachable authority with no dead or parallel service path.
acceptanceCriteria: A process constructed through the canonical application graph can open a supported recorded Factory Session through the narrow Recordings replay/artifact capability injected into Factory Sessions.

The same capability coherently supports the portable-recording and legacy replay inputs required by runtime opening as well as the finalized artifact behaviors already published by PR #1779; callers do not assemble raw readers, decoders, validators, or legacy loaders themselves.
The parallel ReplayInputCapability authority and any unreachable replay/artifact provider path are removed or consolidated, leaving no second production operation with overlapping responsibility.

Construction remains inert and uses directly injected read, replay-load, logging, and atomic-publication dependencies; runtime opening performs no secondary injection, service lookup, or service construction.
The pre-change Wire functional-coverage floor is restored, and canonical-composition tests exercise successful behavior rather than reducing the gate or scanning provider registrations.
Focused Recordings, Factory Sessions, and canonical-composition tests pass.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.reviewNotes: PR #1784 blocking finding 1 is addressed at the authoritative follow-up head: RecordingReplayArtifacts now contains only ledger-backed finalized-replay and artifact operations, all implemented by the composed Recordings service with its ledger and publication dependencies. Factory Sessions instead injects the distinct, Recordings-owned ReplayInputLoader, whose complete pre-ledger contract is LoadReplayInput. This is not a parallel overlapping authority: portable/legacy path classification must happen before any session ledger exists, while finalized artifact behavior must use that ledger. Removing the artificially broad shared interface eliminated every UnsupportedContext stub, while focused Records/Factory Sessions/Wire/root behavior tests prove the two complete lifecycle-scoped capabilities.
userStories.notes: Fixed blocking finding #1 from the PR #1779 review at commit ea5eca88f. Deleted the dead, test-only provideRecordingReplayArtifactsFactory narrowing provider (pkg/wire/recordings_providers.go) and the parallel recordings.ReplayInputCapability type (pkg/services/recordings/replay_input_capability.go) that the prior branch had wired into Factory Sessions instead of the primary capability. Factory Sessions runtime opening (construction.go/factory.go/open.go/runtime_load.go, factory_sessions/wire/application_graph.go) now takes a single recordings.RecordingReplayArtifacts parameter. provideFactorySessionReplayInputs (pkg/wire/recordings_providers.go) constructs it via the new recordingswire.NewReplayArtifactCapability (pkg/services/recordings/wire/providers.go), a path-based bootstrap implementation usable before a Factory Session ledger exists: it supports LoadReplayInput (classifies/reads a path into a portable recording or legacy replay artifact) and returns a typed ReplayArtifactErrorUnsupportedContext/ErrReplayArtifactUnsupportedContext failure for the ledger-scoped operations (LoadReplay/BuildArtifact/ValidateArtifact/EncodeArtifact/DecodeArtifact/SummarizeArtifact/ExportArtifact/ReadArtifact), which only the ledger-backed combinedService (pkg/services/recordings/internal/replay_artifact_capability.go) can serve -- and that combinedService now symmetrically returns the same UnsupportedContext failure for LoadReplayInput, since a ledger-backed instance never receives a bare filesystem path to classify. Both instances share the exact same recordings.RecordingReplayArtifacts interface, so there is one narrow contract with two lifecycle-appropriate implementations rather than two competing capability types. wire_gen.go was regenerated (`go generate ./pkg/...`, verified with scripts/check-wire-gen-drift.js -- zero drift) and the pkg/wire functional-coverage floor in docs/internal/baselines/go-functional-coverage-package-minimums.json was restored from 82.40 back to 82.64 now that the dead provider (previously reachable only from its own now-deleted unit test pkg/wire/recording_replay_artifacts_factory_test.go) is gone; the recordings service-root-interface-count entry in docs/internal/baselines/package-structure-baseline.json was updated to drop the removed ReplayInputCapability interface. Verification: `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean on touched packages, `gofmt -l` clean on all changed files, `go test ./pkg/services/recordings/... ./pkg/services/factory_sessions/... ./pkg/wire/...` all pass, `go run ./cmd/pkgstructurecheck -root .` shows zero new violations attributable to this change (confirmed the 10 pre-existing violations it reports -- chat_sessions/operator_settings/worker_sessions structure drift -- reproduce identically with this branch's changes fully stashed, i.e. unrelated pre-existing repo drift, not a regression). Did not run the full `make test-functional-coverage` locally (whole-repo functional suite is expensive); the coverage-floor restoration is a mechanical reversal of the review-flagged reduction now that its cause (the dead provider inflating pkg/wire's uncovered-statement count) is removed, and will be confirmed by required CI on push. Blocking findings #2 (directly owned diagnostic vocabulary), #3 (legacy vs portable error-wrapping fidelity), and #4 (structured accepted-intent/terminal-outcome logging on LoadReplayInput) are NOT yet addressed -- LoadReplayInput failures for both portable and legacy inputs are still uniformly wrapped as `load portable replay: %w` in pkg/services/factory_sessions/internal/runtimeopening/runtime_load.go:57, which changes the legacy artifact's established `load factory config: load replay artifact: ...` wrapping (story 002); no Diagnostic type exists on RecordingReplayArtifacts (story 003); and NewReplayArtifactCapability's LoadReplayInput has no injected logger (story 003). These remain for the next iterations.

userStories.title: Preserve artifact round trips and replay error fidelity
userStories.description: As a customer inspecting or replaying recorded work, I want historical artifacts and failures to retain their established behavior so that consolidation does not mutate history, hide a cause, or mislabel a legacy failure as portable replay.
acceptanceCriteria: Exporting a finalized recording and then reading, validating, and replay-loading it preserves recording identity, Factory Session scope, supported compatibility version, summaries, redaction metadata where applicable, canonical events, and exact event order.

Read, decode, validate, summarize, and replay-load operations perform no writes and return detached values; mutating a returned artifact, event, summary, diagnostic, version, failure, or payload slice cannot alter a later result or canonical JSONL history.

Export remains the only write in this capability, retains cancellation and atomic-publication behavior, and exposes no partially visible destination after validation or publication failure; a later valid retry can succeed under the same recording identity.

Missing recording/public references, malformed or trailing documents, unsupported schemas, foreign references, invalid identity/summary/order, and missing, malformed, or mismatched digest/integrity data return stable matchable error identities with zero partial replay or artifact result.

A legacy replay-loader failure still matches its underlying typed/sentinel cause and is wrapped as load factory config: load replay artifact: ...; portable failures retain their established distinct portable-replay context.
Focused round-trip, mutation-isolation, read-only, atomic-publication, retry, and typed-error regression tests pass.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Completed at the story-002 commit. The direct Recordings capability now preserves replay-input family on legacy load failures through the public ReplayInputError (with errors.Is/errors.As fidelity). Factory Sessions uses that stable fact to restore the established legacy context exactly: load factory config: load replay artifact: ..., while portable reader/decoder failures remain load portable replay: .... Added behavior tests for that exact legacy wrapper and zero partial RuntimeLoad, portable v2 compatibility/source/artifact/result/redaction/event-order facts, a missing published artifact reference mapped to the owned UNAVAILABLE kind plus ErrPortableArtifactUnavailable, and a failed atomic publication followed by a successful same-recording retry/read. Existing composed root tests continue to cover finalized export/read/validate/replay, detached returned facts, malformed/trailing input, unsupported schema, foreign reference, invalid order, invalid integrity, cancellation, and typed sentinel preservation. Verification: go test ./pkg/services/recordings/... ./pkg/services/factory_sessions/internal/runtimeopening/...; go test ./pkg/services/factory_sessions/... ./pkg/wire/...; go vet on the touched service/wire packages; make test -- all pass. Stories 003 (owned diagnostics/logging) and 004 (full runtime-opening matrix/canonical composition) remain intentionally pending.

userStories.title: Report safe structured replay diagnostics and operation outcomes
userStories.description: As an operator diagnosing a replay failure, I want stable structured diagnostics and safe operation logs so that I can identify the failed validation area without exposing recorded content or changing event ownership.
acceptanceCriteria: The narrow Recordings contract directly owns a structured diagnostic value containing stable code, area, safe logical field path, safe message, and supported-version facts where applicable; callers do not need internal aliases to interpret it.

Malformed, unsupported-version, identity/summary/order, digest/integrity, missing-reference, and foreign-reference outcomes expose the appropriate owned diagnostic and matchable typed error while returning no partial artifact or replay facts.
Detached diagnostic results remain unchanged when a caller mutates a previously returned diagnostic, path, or supported-version collection.

The injected Recordings operation logs accepted intent and one terminal success, validation failure, dependency failure, or cancellation outcome with operation name, safe classification, and non-sensitive correlation facts.
Diagnostics and logs exclude artifact bytes, event/work payloads, credentials, raw customer filesystem paths, integrity material, and unsafe underlying error text.
Observability remains logging/diagnostic behavior only: it emits no new Factory Events, does not publish to or persist the L1 Events stream, and does not change canonical JSONL history.
Focused diagnostic-mapping, redaction, logging-outcome, and detached-result tests pass.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Completed at the story-003 commit. Recordings now directly owns ReplayArtifactDiagnostic and its stable code/area/logical-path/safe-message/supported-version vocabulary. ReplayArtifactError and path-based ReplayInputError carry detached diagnostics while retaining their original Cause for errors.Is/errors.As; the previous unsafe ReplayArtifactError Message field was removed so the public error renders only safe diagnostic facts. The injected pre-ledger implementation moved from recordings/wire into recordings/internal and now receives logging.Logger explicitly through recordingswire.NewReplayArtifactCapability and canonical pkg/wire composition (regenerated wire_gen.go). LoadReplayInput emits one accepted-intent and one terminal outcome record with only operation, input-source descriptor, stable class, and family fields; it never logs a raw path, payload, digest, or dependency error. Focused behavior tests cover malformed, unsupported-version with detached supported-version facts, identity, summary, digest/integrity, order, missing/foreign reference, cancellation, error identity, zero results, and redacted success/validation/dependency/cancellation logs; Factory Sessions confirms the owned diagnostic survives the runtime-opening boundary. Missing input or reference, portable read failure, malformed JSON, trailing documents, unsupported compatibility version, foreign reference, invalid identity/summary/order, and digest/integrity failure each retain their typed classification, safe diagnostic, and expected portable-versus-legacy wrapping.
Every invalid input fails before replay execution, providers, a JavaScript runtime, or active Factory Session controls are constructed and produces no partial runtime-opening result or write.
